s1.syndrome_frame: A clinical presentation of severe fatigue, muscular weakness, and cachexia with a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger, associated with hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient exhibits significant muscular weakness
Patient is cachectic
Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Tumor has gradually enlarged in recent months
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, and a tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathology showing fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells

shortlist.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, elevated parathyroid hormone levels, and hypercalcemia

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a large tumor, elevated parathyroid hormone levels, and hypercalcemia, which could be indicative of parathyroid carcinoma

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, and radiography showing complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption

raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, elevated serum parathyroid hormone, hypercalcemia, and hypophosphatemia, combined with the presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger and radiographic findings of bone resorption, are consistent with the development of a brown tumor, a known complication of hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, this diagnosis alone does not explain the tumor on the finger or the specific radiographic findings.

rejected.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided in the vignette to suggest parathyroid carcinoma, such as a parathyroid gland mass or metastasis.

rejected.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
rejected.why: Osteitis fibrosa cystica is a condition associated with hyperparathyroidism, but it is more of a generalized skeletal process rather than a localized tumor like the one described on the finger.

rejected.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is characterized by the presence of jaw tumors, which are not mentioned in the vignette, and typically involves a familial component, which is not indicated in the patient's history.
